values: As a parent, I want to register and sign in using my email address and password so that I can securely access Babysteps and manage my children's learning profiles.

Babysteps shall support parent account registration and login using only email address and password in Version 1. Immediately after Supabase Auth successfully creates the user, the platform shall create exactly one parent profile linked one-to-one with that Auth user. The profile may exist while email verification is pending, but protected parent and learner data shall remain inaccessible until the email is verified. Profile creation shall be idempotent and recoverable.

1. Version 1 supports email and password only; Google, Apple, phone and magic-link authentication are excluded.
2. Email is the unique login identifier and is normalized before submission.
3. Password storage, hashing and verification remain entirely within Supabase Auth.
4. A parent profile is created immediately after the Auth user is created.
5. Email verification is required before protected parent or learner data can be accessed.
6. One Supabase Auth user maps to exactly one parent profile.
7. Repeated signup callbacks, triggers, refreshes or recovery calls must not create duplicate parent profiles.
8. Suspended or deleted profiles cannot access protected resources.
9. A child learner does not require an Auth user or email account.
The visitor is not authenticated. The Babysteps Supabase project, authentication email provider and callback URLs are configured.
The visitor submits the registration form or login form.

Registration:
1. Parent enters email, password and password confirmation.
2. Client and server validate the inputs.
3. Supabase Auth creates the authentication identity.
4. A database trigger or trusted server process creates the parent profile immediately with onboarding_status='profile_pending'.
5. A verification email is sent.
6. Parent verifies the email.
7. On first verified access, Babysteps confirms the existing profile and continues to parent-profile onboarding.

Login:
1. Parent enters email and password.
2. Supabase Auth validates the credentials.
3. Babysteps checks email verification and parent profile status.
4. If the profile is unexpectedly missing, a recovery upsert creates it safely.
5. Parent enters the account area or resumes the next incomplete onboarding step.

Exact build packet: 09_Codex_Build_Specs!CBS-IA-001
Mandatory parent mobile number with optional display name
As a registered parent, I want to complete a minimal parent profile so that Babysteps can identify and contact me without collecting unnecessary personal information.

After email verification, Babysteps shall require the parent to complete the existing parent profile by supplying a valid mobile number. The display name shall be optional. Mobile numbers shall be format-validated and normalized only; Version 1 shall not send or require an SMS OTP. Postal address and parent date of birth shall not be collected. Invoices and receipts shall be delivered to the authenticated email address. The invoice recipient label shall use the display name when present and the email address when the display name is absent.

1. The parent profile already exists before onboarding begins.
2. Mobile number is mandatory before the parent can continue to learner setup.
3. Mobile number must be parsed and validated using the selected country or calling code.
4. Store the normalized mobile number in E.164 format.
5. Version 1 performs format validation only; it does not send an SMS OTP and does not mark the number as verified.
6. Mobile number does not have to be globally unique because family members may share a contact number.
7. Display name is optional and may be blank.
8. Email is read-only and comes from Supabase Auth.
9. Postal address, parent date of birth and legal name are not collected in Version 1.
10. Invoices and receipts are sent to the authenticated email address.
11. Invoice recipient label uses display name when present; otherwise it uses the authenticated email address.
12. Mobile number use for marketing or SMS requires separate consent and is outside this requirement.
13. Successful completion changes onboarding_status from profile_pending to learner_pending.
14. Repeated submissions update the same profile and do not create duplicate consent records.
The parent has a verified Supabase session, an active parent profile and onboarding_status='profile_pending'. Current Terms of Service and Privacy Policy versions are configured.
The verified parent enters or resumes parent-profile onboarding.

7. Client and server validate the mobile number using country-aware rules.
8. Server stores the number in E.164 format and updates the existing profile.
9. Versioned policy acceptance records are written idempotently.
10. onboarding_status changes to learner_pending.
11. Continue directly to learner-profile creation.

Exact build packet: 09_Codex_Build_Specs!CBS-IA-002
Parent credential changes and soft account deletion
As a parent, I want to safely change my password or login email and deactivate my account so that I can maintain control of my Babysteps identity without permanently deleting retained records.

Babysteps shall allow an authenticated active parent to change the account password, request a login-email change and soft-delete the account. Email changes require current-password reauthentication and verification of the proposed new email. The verification link expires exactly 24 hours after issue. The current email remains active until verification succeeds. Immediately after successful verification, the new email becomes the authoritative login, invoice and receipt address, and the previous email is archived. Account deletion is a soft delete only: records remain in the database, all access is blocked and active sessions are revoked. Restoration is administrator-controlled and never self-service in Version 1.

1. Credential changes require an authenticated, verified and active parent profile.
2. The current password must be revalidated immediately before password change, email-change request or account soft deletion.
3. New passwords must meet the central policy, match confirmation and differ from the current password.
4. The new email must be normalized, valid, different from the current email and unused by another Auth identity.
5. Supabase Secure Email Change must be disabled so only the proposed new email requires verification.
6. Auth email-link expiry must be configured to 86,400 seconds.
7. While verification is pending, the current email remains the active login and invoice address.
8. On successful email verification, the new email activates immediately and the old email is archived.
9. Expired, cancelled or failed email changes leave the current email unchanged.
10. Only one pending email-change request may exist per parent.
11. Soft delete sets account_status='deleted', deleted_at and auth_revoked_before; it never physically deletes Auth, profile, learner, progress, consent, billing, invoice or audit records.
12. Soft deletion revokes all Babysteps parent, learner and app sessions.
13. Platform middleware denies deleted accounts even if a Supabase Auth session can still be established.
14. Deleted accounts cannot self-restore. An authorized platform administrator may restore the account, after which the parent must sign in again.
15. Every subscription belongs to its purchaser parent through purchaser_parent_id. Subscription cancellation and financial retention are governed by Billing; this requirement emits an account_soft_deleted event but does not silently delete financial records.
IA-001 and IA-002 are implemented. The parent has a verified Supabase identity, an active profile and completed profile onboarding. Supabase email delivery and callback URLs are configured.

Password change:
1. Parent enters current password, new password and confirmation.
2. Server reauthenticates the current email/password using an isolated non-persistent Supabase client.
3. Server validates the new password.
4. Auth password is updated.
5. Success is shown and the action is audited.

Email change:
1. Parent enters proposed email and current password.
2. Server reauthenticates and validates uniqueness/format.
3. A pending email-change record is created.
4. Supabase Auth updateUser({email:newEmail}) sends verification to the new email only.
5. Current email remains active.
6. Verification callback validates the Supabase email_change token within 24 hours.
7. Callback confirms the Auth user now has the new email.
8. Old email is inserted into parent_email_history and request is marked verified.
9. Sessions are refreshed; new email becomes login/invoice email immediately.
10. A reconciliation action completes archival if Auth changed but callback persistence was interrupted.

Soft delete:
1. Parent reviews retained-data warning and enters current password plus DELETE confirmation.
2. Server reauthenticates.
3. In one platform transaction, set deleted status/timestamps, revoke platform sessions and write audit/outbox events.
4. Sign the browser out and show the deleted-account confirmation.
5. Subsequent platform access is denied.

Exact build packet: CBS-IA-003
Windows Hello and Apple passkey access for learners
As a parent, I want to enroll a learner for passkey access on compatible Windows and Mac devices so that the child can enter Babysteps without using the parent's email and password.

Babysteps may provide optional learner access using standards-based WebAuthn passkeys backed by the operating system platform authenticator. On Windows, the local verification experience may be Windows Hello PIN, face or fingerprint. On macOS, it may be Touch ID, device passcode or another Apple passkey flow. Babysteps shall never receive or store the operating-system PIN or biometric. A parent must authenticate and enroll the learner first. A successful passkey assertion creates only a restricted learner session and never grants parent, billing or administrative access.

1. This feature is Nice to Have and must not block Version 1 launch.
2. Use WebAuthn/passkeys, not a Babysteps-owned Windows or Mac PIN.
3. Enrollment requires an active verified parent, completed onboarding and recent current-password reauthentication.
4. The selected learner must be owned by the parent or explicitly shared with that parent through learner-level authorization, and must be active.
5. Registration and authentication occur only on the central account origin.
6. Production RP ID is account.babysteps.in; production origin is https://account.babysteps.in. Local/preview environments use separately configured valid RP IDs/origins.
7. Registration requests authenticatorAttachment='platform', residentKey='required', userVerification='required' and attestation='none'.
8. Server challenges are random, single-use and expire after five minutes.
9. Store only WebAuthn credential material and metadata; never store PINs, biometric templates or platform secrets.
10. One learner may have multiple active passkeys; every credential can be individually named and revoked by an authorized parent.
11. Successful authentication creates a learner-only session scoped to the selected learner.
12. Learner passkey sessions cannot access parent account settings, billing, learner-management administration or another learner.
13. The one-active-learner-session rule still applies.
14. If passkeys are unavailable, cancelled or fail, fallback is parent email/password login; do not create a custom child PIN here.
15. Apple passkeys may synchronize through iCloud Keychain; do not promise that a credential is restricted to one physical Mac.
16. Signature-counter anomalies are evaluated according to passkey behavior; zero/non-incrementing counters for synced passkeys are logged rather than automatically treated as cloning.
IA-001 through IA-003, learner profiles, learner authorization, app-launch/session control and WebAuthn-capable HTTPS origins are implemented.

Enrollment:
1. Parent signs in and reauthenticates with current password.
2. Parent selects an active learner they own or are authorized to manage.
3. Parent gives the credential a friendly label.
4. Server creates one-time registration options and stores a challenge.
5. Browser calls navigator.credentials.create through a WebAuthn library.
6. Windows Hello or Apple platform authenticator performs local user verification.
7. Server verifies challenge, origin, RP ID hash, attestation response and user-verification flag.
8. Store credential ID, public key, counter and metadata.
9. Show enrolled credential and revocation controls.

Learner authentication:
1. Open central Child access screen.
2. Select learner profile.
3. Server creates authentication options limited to that learner's non-revoked credentials.
4. Browser calls navigator.credentials.get.
5. Platform authenticator performs local verification.
6. Server verifies challenge, origin, RP ID, signature, credential ownership and UV flag.
7. Update counter/last-used metadata.
8. Create or refresh only a restricted learner authentication session.
9. Continue to the unified launcher. LP-004 independently authorizes learning-session start and must never revoke or replace an ongoing learning session.

Learner profile creation and direct parent ownership

As a verified parent, I want to create a learner profile for any person—including myself—with a unique familiar name and date of birth so that every Babysteps app can identify the learner consistently and tailor presentation appropriately.

Babysteps shall allow an authenticated, verified and active parent to create one or more learner profiles for children, adults or the parent themselves. Every learner shall receive a permanent UUID and exactly one owner_parent_id derived from the authenticated parent profile. Display name and date of birth are mandatory; an approved platform avatar is optional. Learner display names must be unique across every learner permanently owned by the parent. There is no maximum learner age and learner creation must not be rejected because the learner is an adult. The learner profile shall not receive a separate email, password, phone number or Supabase Auth identity. Learner creation is independent of subscriptions, entitlements and app progress.

1. owner_parent_id comes only from the authenticated server session and is never accepted from the client.
2. A parent may own multiple learners and may create a learner profile for themselves.
3. Every learner has exactly one primary owner. A self-learner profile is still a separate learner record owned by the same parent profile.
4. Display name is mandatory, 1–50 visible characters and stored using the parent's preferred capitalization.
5. Before uniqueness comparison, normalize with Unicode NFKC, trim leading/trailing whitespace, collapse internal whitespace runs to one space and apply locale-independent case folding.
6. unique(owner_parent_id, normalized_display_name) applies across every learner permanently owned by the parent. Learner records are not paused, archived, hidden or deleted in Version 1.
7. Date of birth is mandatory, stored as a PostgreSQL date and must be a valid non-future date.
8. There is no maximum learner age. Learner creation accepts any valid past date of birth supported by the database. Age must not be used as an eligibility gate.
9. Do not persist a separate age field. Calculate ageYears and ageMonths from date_of_birth and an explicit ageAsOfDate.
10. Raw date of birth is visible only to the owning parent, authorized support/admin roles and trusted platform services. Learning apps receive derived ageYears, ageMonths and ageAsOfDate by default, not raw date of birth.
11. Age may tailor vocabulary, explanation length, visual density, scaffolding, narration and delivery speed. Age must never override prerequisites, demonstrated mastery, remediation or advancement.
12. Avatar is optional and must reference an active approved platform avatar. Learner photo upload is excluded.
13. The learner record has no lifecycle status field.
14. The first successful learner creation changes parent onboarding_status from learner_pending to complete in the same transaction.
15. Learner creation succeeds without any subscription. No subscription, entitlement, session allowance or app-progress row is created.
16. The create operation requires a parent-scoped idempotency key. Repeating an already successful request returns the same learner.
17. When the owning parent is suspended or soft deleted, all access to owned learner profiles—including a self-learner profile—is denied. Learner records remain retained.
18. A restored parent must establish a new login session before learner access resumes.
19. Additional guardians, when implemented, receive explicit learner-level permissions and do not replace owner_parent_id automatically.
20. No separate relationship or household field is required to indicate that a learner is the parent; the direct owner relationship and learner record remain sufficient for Version 1.

As the owning parent, I want to correct a learner's display name, date of birth or avatar without changing the learner's identity, access history or learning progress.

Babysteps shall allow the authenticated owning parent to correct an existing learner profile's display name, date of birth and approved avatar. Corrections shall preserve the learner UUID, owner_parent_id, subscriptions, entitlements, progress, mastery, placement, session history and weekly usage. Learner profiles are permanent identities and Version 1 shall provide no pause, archive, restore, hide, merge, transfer or delete operation.

1. Only display_name, date_of_birth and avatar_id are editable.
2. learner.id, owner_parent_id, created_at, progress, mastery, subscription assignment, entitlement state and weekly session usage are immutable through this requirement.
3. Name corrections use the exact LP-001 normalization and parent-scoped uniqueness rules.
4. A capitalization or display-format correction is allowed when the normalized name remains owned by the same learner.
5. A name matching another learner owned by the parent is rejected.
6. Date of birth must be a valid, non-future PostgreSQL date. There is no maximum learner age.
7. Correcting date of birth recalculates derived age context for future sessions but never resets placement, mastery, completed work, progress or weekly usage.
8. An app session already in progress retains its learner-context snapshot; revised age context applies from the next app launch/session.
9. avatar_id may be changed to another active approved avatar or set to null. Learner photo upload remains excluded.
10. Each learners row has version integer not null default 1.
11. Every mutation requires expectedVersion and a parent+learner-scoped idempotencyKey.
12. A successful material correction increments version exactly once.
13. An exact no-op returns the current learner without incrementing version or writing a change event.
14. Same idempotency key and same payload returns the original completed result; same key with a different payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
15. Concurrent stale updates return LEARNER_VERSION_CONFLICT and never overwrite newer data.
16. A successful correction writes one learner_profile_changed event containing learner ID, actor parent ID, changed field names, previous version, new version and timestamp. Routine audit events do not duplicate raw DOB or display-name values.
17. Suspended or soft-deleted parent accounts cannot read or correct any learner profile.
18. Learner correction does not create, cancel, reassign or modify subscriptions or entitlements.
19. There is no parent-facing or admin-facing learner deletion path in LP-002.
20. All corrections are transactional and strict-schema validated; protected or unknown fields are rejected.

Active learner selection, scheduled app launch and interruption-safe sessions

As a parent and learner, we want to select the correct learner, open only that learner's scheduled subscribed app, prevent simultaneous use of one learner profile, and safely resume an accidentally interrupted 45-minute session without consuming another weekly session.

Babysteps shall establish an explicit, server-authorized learner context before app launch. A parent with more than one learner must select a learner; a parent with exactly one learner may have that learner selected automatically. The learner home shall show only the selected learner's entitled apps and enable session start only for the app currently authorized by the central schedule. Each learner may have at most one active or resumable learning session across all apps and devices. No user override of an ongoing session is permitted. A session interrupted by accidental browser closure, crash or connectivity loss may resume as the same session on the original device/browser within a 15-minute cumulative recovery allowance. Each learner receives two normal 45-minute sessions per week per entitled app; sessions are consumed at start, and any additional replacement session requires an audited administrator credit based on session logs.

1. A parent owning more than one learner must explicitly select a learner before entering learner home or seeing launchable apps.
2. A parent owning exactly one learner may be auto-selected after authentication. Zero learners routes to learner creation.
3. Learner selection is stored only for the current authenticated parent session and is cleared on logout, session expiry or account change. A multi-learner account must select again after a new login.
4. The selected learner must be carried by immutable learner UUID through learner home, schedule authorization, app launch, learning-session token, heartbeats and progress writes. Display name or browser state is never authoritative.
5. Learner home returns only the selected learner's entitlements, weekly usage and schedule state. Other learners' commercial or progress data is never mixed into the response.
6. Entitled apps may be displayed for orientation, but Start is enabled only for an app carrying a current server-issued schedule authorization. LP-004 consumes the schedule decision and does not calculate pedagogy or scheduling order.

8. Each learner may have at most one learning session in starting, active or disconnected/resumable state across all apps and devices.
9. Consequently, a parent owning N learner profiles can have at most N simultaneous reserved learning sessions, with no more than one belonging to each learner. Parent dashboard/authentication sessions do not count.
10. Different learners owned by the same parent may learn simultaneously on different devices when each independently passes entitlement, scheduling and weekly-capacity checks.
11. If the same learner is selected on another device while a session is active or resumable, display a session-in-progress popup and reject a new start. Do not offer takeover, override or End other session.
12. Starting a different app for the same learner is also blocked while any learning session for that learner is active or resumable.
13. A normal qualifying session start atomically consumes the next of two weekly slots for the learner_id + app_id + week_key. Retries with the same idempotency key return the same session and never consume twice.
14. Weekly capacity is two normal sessions per learner per app. A bundle retains a separate two-session allowance for each included app.
15. The week key is calculated server-side using the learner's stored timezone and ISO week beginning Monday 00:00. It is persisted at session start and is never client supplied. A timezone change may take effect only at the next week boundary.
16. A learning session provides at most 2,700 seconds of connected session time. Disconnected recovery time does not count toward the 45-minute session clock.
17. The app sends an authenticated heartbeat every 30 seconds. The server records last_heartbeat_at, connected_elapsed_seconds and verified_active_seconds; each heartbeat may add no more than the elapsed server interval and never trusts a client-total counter.
18. On an authenticated close/pagehide beacon, crash, connection loss or missed heartbeat, the session becomes disconnected/resumable. The server uses the close beacon when received; otherwise it derives disconnection from the last confirmed heartbeat.
19. The same session may resume only on the original device/browser using its valid device binding and resume credential.
20. The first interruption allows resume until disconnected_at + 15 minutes. Across repeated interruptions, cumulative disconnected time may not exceed 900 seconds; the effective deadline is limited by the remaining cumulative allowance.
21. Resume preserves session_id, learner_id, app_id, week_key and weekly slot number. It does not create a session row, consume a weekly slot or change the scheduled app.
22. During the recovery window, the learner session remains reserved and blocks every new start for that learner on every device.
23. If resume does not occur before the deadline, a server sweeper or the next session operation finalizes the session as interrupted, releases the learner lock and rejects future resume attempts.
24. Session states are starting, active, disconnected, completed, interrupted, expired and revoked_by_admin. There is no superseded or user-overridden state.
25. A session is conclusively considered used when verified_active_seconds is at least 1,350 seconds, which is 50% of 45 minutes. It is ineligible for a replacement credit.
26. A session below 1,350 verified active seconds remains consumed by default and is never restored automatically. The parent may contact support, and an administrator may grant one audited replacement credit only after reviewing platform logs and confirming a credible technical interruption.
27. A replacement credit is tied to one original session, learner and app; one original session may produce at most one credit. The credit does not alter or delete the original session.
28. A valid unused replacement credit authorizes one additional session for the same learner and app without increasing the two normal slots. It still requires valid entitlement, schedule authorization and no concurrent learner session.
29. Admin credit creation and evidence workflow are implemented in the Administration building block. LP-004 defines and consumes the replacement-credit contract.
30. Closing voluntarily, switching devices, attempting a concurrent start or remaining idle does not automatically qualify for a replacement credit.
31. When a parent account is suspended or soft deleted, selection and learner-home access are denied and all learning-session tokens stop working according to IA-003.
32. Progress writes require the active session token and exact learner/app binding. Completed, interrupted, expired, revoked or foreign tokens are rejected.
33. App session and progress ownership never changes when the parent switches the launcher to another learner.
34. There is no API, UI or hidden parameter that lets a parent or learner override an ongoing session.

Admin-managed canonical app registration and soft deletion

As an authorized platform administrator, I want to register and manage Babysteps learning apps through a dedicated admin page so every platform relationship uses one permanent app identity and an app can be removed from operation without deleting its identity or historical references.

Babysteps shall provide a Version 1 App Registry administration page and privileged APIs for creating, viewing and editing app registrations, activating draft apps, soft-deleting apps and restoring soft-deleted apps. Every app receives one permanent UUID and one globally unique immutable app_key. Soft deletion is the only deletion mechanism; no hard-delete operation exists. Soft deletion immediately blocks new operational activity while retaining the minimal app identity required to interpret existing references.

1. The dedicated admin route is /admin/apps with create, details, edit, activate, soft-delete and restore actions.
2. Only an authenticated administrator with the relevant app-registry permission may use registry mutation APIs.
3. Public users, parents, learners, browser apps and learning-app services cannot self-register or mutate app records.
4. Every app has an immutable UUID primary key and immutable globally unique app_key.
5. app_key is lowercase ASCII, hyphen separated, begins with a letter, contains only a-z, 0-9 and hyphen, and is 2–50 characters: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,49}$.
6. display_name is required, trimmed plain text, 1–80 visible characters and may be rebranded without changing app identity.
7. short_description is required before activation, plain text only and 1–240 characters.
8. icon_asset_key must reference an active approved platform asset before activation. Arbitrary remote icon URLs are prohibited.
9. category and owning_team are required before activation and are mutable descriptive metadata only.
10. Initial registry states are draft, active and soft_deleted.
11. A new app is created in draft. Draft apps cannot be mapped to commercial products, granted as entitlements, scheduled or launched.
12. Activation requires complete valid metadata and environment configuration readiness supplied by AR-002; activation is version checked and audited.
13. The initial Chess Master, Magical Math and Speed Reader apps shall be registered through the same admin-controlled service. A bootstrap script may call the service idempotently but must not bypass its validation or identity rules.
14. All subscriptions, product mappings, entitlements, schedules, sessions, progress and analytics aggregates reference app_registry.id through app_id.
15. app_key may be used in URLs/configuration, but database foreign keys and authorization use app_id.
16. Unknown app IDs and app keys fail closed. No entitlement, progress, analytics or launch request implicitly creates an app.
17. Mutable fields are display_name, short_description, icon_asset_key, category, owning_team and internal operational notes.
18. Immutable fields are id, app_key and created_at. Attempted mutation is rejected.
19. Every app row has version integer not null default 1; material mutations require expectedVersion and increment version exactly once.
20. Every mutation requires an administrator-scoped idempotency key. Same key and same payload returns the original result; different payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
21. Soft deletion is the only delete action. There is no hard-delete API, UI, SQL function or normal operational procedure.
22. Soft deletion requires recent administrator reauthentication, app_registry_soft_delete permission, a mandatory reason code, optional concise reason note and exact typed confirmation of the app_key.
23. Soft deletion atomically sets registry_status=soft_deleted, records soft_deleted_at, invalidates active launch/schedule authorizations and emits app_soft_deleted.
24. Soft deletion blocks new product mappings, subscriptions for that app, entitlements, schedules, launches, sessions, progress writes and app-originated analytics buffer updates.
25. Soft deletion removes the app from learner and parent launch surfaces but retains app_id, app_key and last display_name so historical references remain interpretable.
26. Soft deletion does not delete learner progress, completed lessons, financial records or already finalized anonymous analytics aggregates; each related table follows its own approved retention policy.
27. Soft deletion does not automatically refund, cancel or reassign subscriptions. Billing requirements own customer remediation.
28. Restore requires app_registry_restore permission, recent reauthentication, reason and expectedVersion.
29. Restore returns the app to draft, not active. Configuration and activation checks must pass again.
30. app_key remains permanently reserved through soft deletion and restoration.
31. App registry reads expose only safe metadata. Secrets, signing keys, environment credentials, private repository URLs and internal incident contacts are excluded.
32. Registry mutations write a minimal audit event with app ID/key, operation, administrator ID, reason code, version transition and timestamp. Do not store duplicate metadata snapshots indefinitely.
33. Routine list queries exclude soft-deleted apps unless includeSoftDeleted=true is requested by an authorized admin.
34. Learning services may read active safe metadata but have no write permission.
35. All changes are transactional and strict-schema validated; unknown and protected fields are rejected.

Exact build packet: CBS-AR-001
As a platform owner, I want one daily aggregation run that answers usage, level-time and age-band questions without retaining permanent learner event histories.

Babysteps shall collect only compact current operational state and one temporary daily analytics buffer row per learner pseudonym, app, level and activity date. At 00:15 Asia/Kolkata, one scheduled job processes the complete previous local calendar day, writes anonymous app-level and level-level aggregates using exact replacement, verifies totals, finalizes the date and deletes all temporary learner-level analytics rows. Permanent analytics tables shall contain no learner UUID, parent UUID, learner name, exact age or date of birth.

1. Standard analytics uses Asia/Kolkata calendar days in Version 1.
2. The daily job runs at 00:15 Asia/Kolkata and receives the explicit previous activity_date; it never infers its target only from server current date.
3. During learning, no raw analytics event, clickstream, page-view, navigation, keystroke, mouse movement, session replay or per-heartbeat row is inserted.
4. Heartbeats update the current learner session row in place. Server-confirmed intervals update one analytics_daily_buffer row in place.
5. Temporary buffer grain is activity_date + learner_daily_key + app_id + level_key.
6. learner_daily_key is HMAC-SHA256 using a dedicated analytics secret over learner_id and activity_date. It changes daily and is deleted with the buffer.
7. The analytics database never receives learner UUID, parent UUID, display name, raw DOB or exact age.
8. Age is derived from restricted DOB for the activity_date and immediately converted to one approved band: under_6, 6_7, 8_9, 10_12, 13_15, 16_18, 19_29, 30_49, 50_plus.
9. Buffer counters are engaged_seconds, sessions_started, sessions_completed, sessions_interrupted and lessons_completed.
10. engaged_seconds is calculated from server-confirmed active intervals and never from a client-submitted total.
11. Each source operation uses a deterministic contribution key or monotonic session checkpoint so retries do not double count.
12. sessions_started belongs to the date of the authoritative server start.
13. sessions_completed and sessions_interrupted belong to the date of finalization.
14. lesson completion belongs to the date the server accepts the idempotent completion.
15. For a session crossing midnight, connected/engaged seconds before midnight update the first date and seconds after midnight update the next date; the learning session and weekly slot remain unchanged.
16. The scheduled run obtains a single-date advisory/distributed lock.
17. The job creates or locks analytics_daily_runs for the target date and refuses concurrent processing.
18. The job reads all buffer rows for the date and calculates level aggregates grouped by date, app_id, level_key and age_band.
19. The job separately calculates app aggregates grouped by date, app_id and age_band directly from buffer rows so an active learner spanning multiple levels is counted once at app grain.
20. Aggregate writes use exact replacement/upsert values, never blind increments.
21. A rerun before deletion or an authorized repair run produces identical aggregate rows for identical buffer contents.
22. Before deletion, the job verifies source and aggregate totals for engaged seconds, sessions started, completed, interrupted and lessons completed.
23. Active learner counts are verified from distinct learner_daily_key at each aggregation grain and are not expected to sum across levels.
24. If any verification fails, aggregate transaction is rolled back or marked failed, the buffer remains intact and an administrator alert is emitted.
25. Only after aggregates are committed and the run is completed may buffer rows and daily pseudonymous keys be deleted.
26. analytics_daily_runs retains only date, state, source row count, source/aggregate control totals, timestamps and failure code; no learner information.
27. Permanent daily aggregates reference immutable app_id. Soft-deleted apps remain interpretable but generate no new buffer updates.
28. Permanent named learner history is limited to the compact learner_app_progress row and lesson_completions required for continuation and parent reporting.
29. learner_app_progress stores only current level/lesson, current unfinished engaged time, current app state, schema/version and updated_at; previous snapshots are not retained indefinitely.
30. lesson_completions stores one row per learner, app and lesson with level_key, completed_at, engaged_seconds and minimal result; no answer-by-answer or session history is required.
31. Standard administrator analytics is cohort based and provides no named-learner drill-down.
32. Anonymous aggregates may be retained for product trend analysis because they contain no learner identifier; retention review remains governed by privacy policy.
33. Current/resumable session data is retained only while operationally required. Finalized session detail is not kept as permanent analytics history.
34. Temporary support evidence required by LP-004 is not analytics data, must remain minimal and follows the explicit support-case retention policy; AN-001 must not duplicate it.
35. No analytics table or job may become the authoritative source for learner progress, weekly usage, entitlement or scheduling decisions.

Exact build packet: CBS-AN-001
Automated app deployment, verified release promotion and rollback

As a platform administrator, I want Babysteps apps to be built, deployed, validated, published and rolled back automatically so learners never depend on manually entered production URLs or unverified releases.

Babysteps shall automate application build, environment deployment, launch-metadata generation, validation, production publication and rollback through a trusted deployment-provider adapter. Administrators bind a registered app to a provider-verified project and approve a release that has already passed staging gates. They never enter or edit a live deployment URL. Each release is an immutable build-once artifact; the same artifact is promoted through staging and production. New learner launches use only the atomically published production deployment, while existing sessions remain bound to the deployment selected at their start. Every production release must be backward compatible with all current platform contracts and every progress schema version present in retained learner progress. Production promotion occurs only inside a pre-scheduled app-specific deployment slot. New learning-session starts are blocked for that app from 60 minutes before the slot until publication or safe rollback completes, and the deployment cannot begin while any starting, active or disconnected/resumable session exists for the app.

1. Version 1 supports development, staging and production deployment environments.
2. The core deployment service uses a provider-neutral DeploymentProvider interface. The initial implementation is a Vercel adapter.
3. Each app may have at most one verified deployment-project binding per environment.
4. A binding is trusted only after the provider API confirms the project exists, belongs to the approved Babysteps provider team, is accessible to the deployment service account and is connected to the expected repository.
5. The same provider project/environment binding cannot be assigned to two app identities.
6. Administrators select from provider-discovered projects and approved Babysteps domains; they cannot type an arbitrary production URL, provider project ID or unapproved domain and have it trusted.
7. The repository contains a version-controlled babysteps.app.json manifest with manifestVersion, appKey, launchPath, returnPath, identityPath, healthPath and minimum supported platform SDK version.
8. The manifest contains no origin, production URL, SSO secret, API key or credential.
9. Manifest appKey must exactly match the immutable registry app_key. Launch/return/identity/health paths are relative same-origin paths, begin with '/', contain no origin, credentials or fragment and pass strict length/character validation.
10. The platform derives the SSO audience from app_key and environment. The application cannot choose an arbitrary audience.
11. A release is created only by an authenticated CI/deployment service for an approved repository commit. Browser administrators cannot register arbitrary source artifacts.
12. Every release has immutable release_id, source commit SHA, dependency-lock hash, build-input hash and artifact digest.
13. Mutable labels such as latest, main or production are never the authoritative release identity.
14. The pipeline builds the artifact once. Staging and production promotion use the exact same artifact digest; production must not rebuild from source.
15. Required build checks include dependency installation from the lockfile, type checking, linting, unit tests, contract tests, security checks and production build success.
16. A failed mandatory check marks the release failed and prevents staging or production promotion.
17. Development/preview deployments use development credentials only, cannot receive production learner tokens or production learner data and expire automatically.
18. A verified release is deployed to staging automatically after build gates pass, or by an authorized explicit staging action when the pipeline is configured for manual staging.
19. Staging validation checks provider success, approved origin, manifest identity, runtime app_id/app_key identity response, health endpoint, launch handshake, SSO audience, callback/return contract, progress contract, session heartbeat contract, exact CORS/message origins, minimum SDK compatibility and basic accessibility smoke tests.
20. A release reaches verified only when every mandatory staging validation passes.
21. Production promotion requires app_deployment_promote permission, recent administrator reauthentication and explicit approval of a specific immutable release.
22. Approval displays app identity, release ID, commit SHA, artifact digest, staging results, current production release and rollback target.
23. Promotion acquires a per-app production lock and revalidates app active status, pipeline enabled state, binding, immutable artifact digest and all required checks.
24. The provider-confirmed production deployment URL/origin is accepted only from the authenticated provider API or verified signed webhook, normalized and matched to an approved Babysteps domain.
25. Browser/admin payloads cannot provide or override the production launch origin.
26. Production smoke validation runs before the platform publishes the deployment to learner launches.
27. If provider deployment or prepublication validation fails, the current published deployment remains unchanged and the failed release is never exposed to new learners.
28. Publication is an atomic update of current_published_deployment_id and previous_healthy_deployment_id for the app/environment.
29. Only a published production deployment may be resolved by the launch service for a new learner session.
30. Every session launch records deployment_id and release_id in its temporary active-session state. Existing active/resumable sessions continue on their original deployment after a new publication.
31. The immediately previous healthy production deployment is retained as the rollback target.
32. After publication, the pipeline performs a ten-minute release-safety observation with one critical check per minute. One identity/SSO-integrity failure or three consecutive critical availability/contract failures triggers automated rollback.
33. Automated rollback atomically restores the previous healthy deployment for new launches, marks the failed deployment rolled_back and alerts administrators. It does not redirect or mutate existing active sessions.
34. Continuous availability and maintenance behavior after the ten-minute release-safety window belongs to AR-003.
35. An authorized administrator may trigger the same automated rollback manually using a specific current deployment and expected publication version.
36. Concurrent production promotions or rollbacks for the same app are serialized; only one may commit.
37. Provider webhooks require signature verification, timestamp tolerance, event-ID idempotency and replay rejection.
38. Deployment provider credentials and environment secrets are stored only in the secrets manager and are separated by environment.
39. Soft-deleted apps and apps with deployment_enabled=false cannot create, promote, publish or roll back to a new deployment.
40. Detailed build logs, provider webhook payloads, preview deployments and repeated validation responses are temporary and automatically purged under explicit retention rules.
41. Babysteps retains only the current published deployment, previous healthy rollback deployment, current verified release awaiting approval, a failed release linked to an open investigation and compact release/promotion audit metadata.
42. Deployment data contains no learner identity or progress data.
43. Every binding, promotion and rollback mutation uses optimistic versioning and administrator/service-scoped idempotency.
44. No direct repository or application credential may change App Registry or publication pointers.
45. All state changes use transactional outbox/audit events and fail without partial publication.
46. Every release must be backward compatible with the currently published platform/app contracts and every schema version present in retained learner_app_progress rows.
47. Compatibility uses expand/migrate/contract sequencing. A production release must not combine a destructive schema removal with code that still depends on the removed shape.
48. Before verification, the pipeline enumerates persisted progress schema versions and runs read/migrate/write compatibility tests for each represented version.
49. A release may write the new schema version only after it can safely read or migrate every represented prior version. Failed migration or rollback-compatibility testing blocks production.
50. Production promotion requires one pre-scheduled app-specific deployment window with starts_at and ends_at.
51. The deployment window must be scheduled at least 60 minutes before starts_at. drain_starts_at is starts_at minus 60 minutes.

Project binding:

Release:
4. CI submits commit SHA, lock hash, build-input hash and idempotency key.
5. Pipeline builds once, calculates artifact digest and runs required checks.
6. Passing artifact is deployed to staging.
7. Platform reads the versioned manifest and validates app identity, routes and integration contracts.
8. Passing release becomes verified and awaits production approval.

Production:
9. Reauthenticated authorized admin reviews the immutable release and approves promotion.
10. Server acquires app production lock and revalidates every gate.
11. Provider promotes the same artifact; platform retrieves and verifies the provider-confirmed origin.
12. Production smoke tests pass.
13. Platform atomically publishes the deployment and records the previous healthy deployment.
14. New sessions use the new deployment; existing sessions retain their original deployment.
15. Ten-minute release-safety checks run.
16. A qualifying critical failure automatically restores the previous healthy publication and alerts administrators.

Retention:
17. Expired previews, superseded staging deployments, detailed logs and processed webhook payloads are purged.
18. Minimum current/rollback/review metadata remains.

Scheduled production window:
19. Admin selects the verified release and schedules an app-specific production slot at least 60 minutes in advance.
20. Platform records drain_starts_at and exposes the block to LP-004.
21. At drain start, new sessions for that app are rejected without usage consumption; existing sessions finish or resume normally.
22. At slot start, the pipeline verifies zero reserved learner sessions for the app.
23. If zero, promotion proceeds using the same artifact. If not, the window is postponed/failed without deployment.
24. Compatibility migrations use expand/migrate/contract and are validated before publication.
25. The app remains start-blocked through production validation and publication/rollback.
26. On safe completion, the block is removed and new sessions may start.

Babysteps Platform and Learning App Backend
As an authorized learner, I want to enter the scheduled learning app without signing in again, while keeping my parent account, learner identity, session allowance and progress securely isolated.

After LP-004 creates or resumes the authoritative learner session, Babysteps shall dispatch the learner to the exact AR-002 deployment using a cryptographically random, single-use, 60-second launch code delivered by cross-origin form POST. The authenticated learning-app backend exchanges the code server-to-server and receives a signed 120-second bootstrap assertion containing only the minimum learner and session context. The app creates its own secure local session. No parent token, reusable learner token, platform refresh token or arbitrary destination is exposed to the browser or app. Launch is blocked during an AR-002 deployment drain/window and consumes no additional allowance.

1. LA-001 starts only after LP-004 has authorized and created/resumed the exact learner_session. It does not recalculate entitlement, schedule, weekly usage or concurrency.
2. AR-001 app_id/app_key and the learner_session's AR-002 deployment_id/release_id are authoritative.
3. The launch service resolves the destination server-side from the session-bound published deployment and validated app manifest.
4. Browser/admin supplied destination, origin, app ID, learner ID, deployment ID or release ID is rejected.
5. No reusable JWT, parent access token, learner token, refresh token or app credential may appear in the launch URL, form or browser storage.
6. The dispatch endpoint returns non-cacheable auto-submitting HTML with a POST form to the exact deployment origin and manifest launch path.
7. Required dispatch headers include no-store/private, no-referrer, nosniff, frame-ancestors none, base-uri none and CSP form-action restricted to the exact origin.
8. The dispatch page loads no analytics, third-party script, image, font or external resource.
9. The launch code is opaque, generated with at least 256 bits of CSPRNG entropy, stored only as a cryptographic hash and expires no later than 60 seconds after creation.
10. One mutable launch-state row exists per active learner session; a retry replaces/revokes the prior unexchanged code and increments attempt_version rather than adding permanent attempt history.
11. The code is bound to learner_session_id, learner_id, app_id, environment, deployment_id, release_id, launch_attempt_id, device_session_id, expiry and attempt_version.
12. The app's POST /launch endpoint must send the code to its backend; browser JavaScript alone cannot validate or consume it.
13. The app backend authenticates to /v1/internal/app-launch/exchange using an environment- and app-bound confidential service identity or workload identity.
14. There is no shared secret across all Babysteps apps.
15. App client assertions expire within 60 seconds, contain unique jti and exact platform exchange audience, and are replay protected.
16. A credential for another app, environment, project or deployment cannot exchange the code.
17. Exchange atomically authenticates the app, validates hash/attempt/expiry/bindings/current session/app state, marks exchanged, clears code hash and issues one bootstrap assertion.
18. Bootstrap assertion expires within 120 seconds and is signed by the Babysteps platform.
19. Bootstrap assertion includes issuer, audience, assertion ID, issue/expiry; app ID/key, environment, deployment/release; learner session ID and learner ID; display name, approved avatar; derived age years/months/as-of date; locale and learner timezone.
20. It excludes raw DOB, parent ID/name/email/mobile, subscription/payment information, other learners, household data, full progress JSON, mastery history and weekly/session-count history.
21. learner_id, learner_session_id and app_id are authoritative. Display name is presentation only.
22. App backend verifies assertion signature, audience, app/deployment/release and expiry before creating an app-local session.
23. App-local cookie is random, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and expires no later than the LP-004 learner session.
24. App-local session cannot grant parent/admin authority, switch learner or launch another app.
25. Exchange uses app-principal-scoped idempotency. Identical retry returns original logical result for a short recovery window; changed request with same key is rejected.
26. A used/revoked/expired code cannot create another app session.
27. Original-device launch retry reuses the same learner_session, weekly slot, scheduled app and deployment, creates a new code and consumes no additional allowance.
28. Another device cannot claim a launch retry.
29. Launch dispatch revalidates account active state, session state/device binding, app active state, deployment binding and AR-002 deployment window.
30. From an app's deployment drain start through safe completion, dispatch/start is blocked with APP_DEPLOYMENT_WINDOW_BLOCKED and consumes no slot, replacement credit, learner session or code.
31. No session may exist during the deployment slot because AR-002 requires zero reserved sessions before deployment.

As a learning-app backend, I want to persist the learner's current continuation state and completed lessons exactly once so progress survives interruptions and future sessions without creating detailed answer or event history.

Babysteps shall store exactly one current progress row per learner and app and exactly one permanent completion row per learner, app and lesson. Authorized app backends may read or atomically replace current progress and may atomically record a first lesson completion together with the next progress state. Progress writes use optimistic versioning, monotonically increasing per-session checkpoint sequence, strict release-registered JSON Schema validation, a 64 KiB serialized-state limit and idempotency. Engaged time and completion timestamps are server authoritative. Babysteps shall not retain previous progress snapshots, answer histories, attempt histories or app-submitted time totals.

1. The learning app owns curriculum, mastery, difficulty, remediation, question generation, lesson correctness and the meaning of its current-state schema.
2. Babysteps owns learner/app/session identity, persistence, authorization, optimistic concurrency, completion uniqueness, server-verified time, data minimization, schema compatibility and analytics contribution.
3. Exactly one learner_app_progress row exists per learner_id + app_id.
4. An accepted checkpoint replaces the previous current state; previous snapshots are not retained.
5. Exactly one lesson_completions row exists per learner_id + app_id + lesson_key.
6. The app obtains learner/app/session/deployment exclusively from LA-002 authorization and cannot submit or override them.
7. First app use returns exists=false and progressVersion=0. The app initializes its own approved initial state.
8. Current progress fields are state_schema_version, level key, lesson key, app-specific state, unfinished lesson/level engaged time, progress_version, last session/checkpoint sequence, state hash and updated time.
9. Each production release registers a versioned JSON Schema and SHA-256 digest for progress state.

Learning-session finalization, secure exit and technical replacement credit
Babysteps Platform and Learning App Backend

As a learner or owning parent, I want a learning session to finish safely with acknowledged progress and, when a technical problem prevented attendance or meaningful completion, receive one time-limited same-app make-up session.

Babysteps shall atomically finalize explicit, time-limit and repeated-interruption learning sessions using the last acknowledged LA-003 progress version, revoke all session-bound authorization, release the learner lock and return the learner safely to Babysteps. Browser close/network loss shall remain resumable rather than normal completion. A distinct third-or-later interruption occurring after server-confirmed connected time exceeds 2,025 seconds shall automatically complete the session. After any consumed finalized session, the learner or owning parent may confirm a technical issue within seven calendar days and receive exactly one same-learner/app technical replacement credit, valid for one calendar month and usable at any time before expiry without normal weekly or schedule consumption.

Centralized deny-by-default authorization and API-only learning-app integration
Parent, Learner, Administrator, Support Agent and Platform Service

As the Babysteps platform, I want every protected action and every platform service consumed by a learning app to pass through authenticated, versioned APIs and one deny-by-default authorization policy so no client, app or service can obtain access by changing identifiers, duplicating route-specific checks or connecting directly to platform infrastructure.

Authentication establishes the actor; the platform resolves the canonical action, exact resource and authoritative context before allowing access. Selected learner context is navigation only and never proof of ownership. Every protected mutation is reauthorized using locked current state. All Babysteps platform services consumed by independently deployed learning apps shall be exposed only through documented, authenticated, authorized and versioned APIs; learning apps and their browsers shall have no direct access to Babysteps databases, authentication administration, tables, functions, queues, private storage or service-role credentials.

1. Default authorization result is deny. An action is allowed only by an explicit active policy rule.
2. Every protected API declares one permanent canonical action_key; browser/app callers cannot choose arbitrary action names.
3. Actor identity and principal type come only from verified parent, learner, administrator, support or managed service authentication.
4. Client-submitted actorId, parentId, role, permission, isAdmin, isOwner or similar authority assertions are rejected or ignored.
5. Authorization evaluates actor, subject and resource separately.
6. Parent selection of a learner is navigation/safety context and is never ownership proof.
7. Learner ownership, app binding, entitlement, session state, deployment state, credit state and lifecycle state come from their authoritative platform services.
8. Permission to one learner/app/resource never implies another.
9. Parent principals remain parents while acting for an owned learner.
10. Learner principals are restricted to their bound learner and cannot access parent profile, billing, learner management, another learner, administrator or support operations.
11. Administrator/support/service permissions are separate from parent and learner authorization and are defined by later BB-05 requirements.
12. Learning-app services remain restricted by LA-002 grant, app/environment/deployment/session binding and fixed scopes.
13. Every protected mutation performs preflight authorization and repeats critical authorization inside the transaction after locking target and relationship rows.
14. The transaction-time decision is authoritative when state changes between preflight and commit.
15. List/search/count APIs build an authorized query scope before loading, pagination, counting or aggregation.
16. Unauthorized rows must not be loaded and then filtered in application memory.
17. Resource-absent and foreign-resource responses are safely non-enumerating.
18. UI capabilities are short-lived hints generated from the same policy and never replace server authorization.
19. Row Level Security and repository scoping are required as defense in depth but do not replace action-level policy.
20. Policy definitions are typed, version controlled, reviewed, tested and promoted as immutable policy bundles.
21. Exactly one authorization policy version is active; activation is atomic and records digest, commit, actor and timestamp.
22. No general browser-editable policy or role-rule editor exists in Version 1.
23. Unknown actions, principal types, resource types, inactive policy, missing mandatory context or policy-service failure fail closed.
24. Mutable authorization state changes become effective within five seconds; no long-lived cached allow decision is permitted.
25. Sensitive actions may require a policy-defined recent reauthentication maximum age.
26. Ordinary allowed reads do not generate permanent per-request audit growth; privileged/sensitive decisions create minimal audit.
27. Authorization logs contain no resource payload, personal data, progress, answers, credentials or tokens.
28. In-process Babysteps modules use one typed authorize/build_authorized_query_scope interface.
29. Separately deployed trusted platform services may call an authenticated internal authorization-decision API.
30. Browser clients and learning apps cannot call the internal authorization-decision endpoint.
31. Babysteps is API-first: every platform capability consumed by a learning application is provided through a documented platform API.
32. Learning applications must not directly access Babysteps PostgreSQL/Supabase tables, database functions, auth administration, queues, private storage or internal event streams.
33. Learning applications and app repositories must never possess Babysteps Supabase service-role keys, direct database credentials or shared cross-app platform secrets.
34. Learning-app browser JavaScript normally calls its own app backend; protected platform calls originate from that backend using LA-002 dual proof.
35. The browser holds only an app-local secure cookie and never receives a Babysteps backend credential.
36. Learning apps may directly serve only their own curriculum, pedagogy and static app-owned JSON/assets.
37. App-owned assets must not contain copied platform personal data, platform credentials or authoritative entitlement/session state.
38. Platform identity, entitlement, session, progress, lesson completion, technical credit, availability/deployment and analytics services are consumed only through approved APIs.
39. API failure must never cause a learning app to fall back to direct database access or locally invent platform state.
40. Every app-facing API contract defines version, strict schemas, authentication, canonical action, authorization context, idempotency, errors, rate limit, audit classification, compatibility and deprecation.
41. Every app release verifies required platform API contracts in staging and remains rollback compatible.
42. A breaking platform API change requires a new version or expand-and-contract migration; supported app releases remain functional during the migration period.
43. Direct-access violations are blocked by CI secret scans, repository policy, database/network controls and automated architecture tests.
44. Adding a new Babysteps platform service requires an approved API contract before any learning app may consume it.
45. Deployment state is authoritative authorization context for learner_session.start, technical_credit.use, launch dispatch and grant creation.
46. During the 60-minute app-specific drain and deployment window, those actions fail closed without consuming a slot, credit, session or launch code.
47. Deployment administrator actions use canonical actions deployment.schedule, reschedule, cancel, promote and rollback with exact app/release binding, recent reauthentication and transactional policy revalidation.
48. Public app downtime begins at the scheduled deployment start and is announced as up to 45 minutes; the preceding 60-minute drain is a new-session preparation pause, not public deployment downtime.
49. The app may reopen earlier after safe publication or rollback.
50. If safe publication/rollback is not complete after 45 minutes, the app remains blocked and the notice changes to an overrun message stating that no session allowance was used.
51. Other apps remain available throughout an app-specific drain/window.
52. Existing frozen identity, learner, deployment, launch, progress and session rules remain authoritative and are consumed rather than recalculated by AU-001.

Browser-local session runtime, signed envelope and hard server expiry

As the Babysteps platform, I want active learning-session liveness and timing to run locally in the original browser under a signed server envelope so learners can recover safely without recurring Supabase reads or writes.

Babysteps shall use one browser-local Session Runtime JSON per active session, protected by a signed immutable session envelope and a fixed server hard expiry. Version 1 shall expose no recurring heartbeat API. Supabase shall be used only for durable business and learning events.

1. Runtime JSON is stored in IndexedDB on the original browser/device.
2. It contains only transient local timer/UI/progress-acknowledgment state.
3. It cannot authorize learner, app, entitlement, slot, credit, deployment or duration.
4. Immutable authority comes from the signed envelope and durable learner_session.
5. Envelope includes session/learner/app/environment/deployment/release/device, usable launch time, hard expiry, 2700-second maximum and version.
6. hard_expires_at equals usable launch plus 3600 seconds.
7. App uses a monotonic timer while foreground and online.
8. App stops local learning at 2700 connected seconds.
9. No recurring heartbeat/poll request exists.
10. No Supabase operation occurs solely because time elapsed.
11. One-tab ownership prevents duplicate local timers.
12. Meaningful progress only; optional five-minute safety checkpoint if meaningful unsaved change exists.
13. Close/offline updates local JSON and may send one best-effort disconnect.
14. Disconnect delivery failure is tolerated; no retry loop.
15. Original browser may resume before hard expiry with envelope/device/resume proof.
16. Other devices cannot resume/take over.
17. Resume reuses source/week/slot/session and last acknowledged progress.
18. Hard expiry finalizes lazily or by sweeper and releases the lock.
19. Accepted reported time is capped by 2700 and possible server wall time.
20. Browser-only unsaved progress is never durable.
21. Runtime JSON clears after finalization or irrecoverable expiry.
22. No runtime/heartbeat history is stored.
23. Repeated-interruption >75% automatic completion is superseded.
24. Technical-credit rules remain unchanged.
25. Revocation/deletion/app state still fails closed on platform calls.
26. App cannot fall back to direct database access.
27. Runtime format is versioned and backward compatible for supported releases.
28. Release tests verify IndexedDB recovery, one-tab ownership and hard expiry.
29. Runtime contains no parent data, raw DOB, subscription/payment or credentials.
30. Signed envelope is verified by the app backend before local session creation.

Eight monthly session credits, next-month expiry and catch-up third-session pacing
Learner, Owning Parent and Session Gateway
As a learner and parent, we want eight standard sessions per subscribed app each month, one-month rollover and a limited catch-up session so unused credits are not unnecessarily lost.

For each eligible learner-app entitlement, Babysteps shall provide eight standard session credits for each calendar month. Unused credits remain valid through the end of the following calendar month. Standard sessions normally remain limited to two per learner, app and calendar week. A third standard session may be authorized only while the learner has more than eight available standard credits and at least one available credit expires at the end of the current month. Credits are consumed earliest-expiry-first and are never pooled across learners or apps. SC-003 reserves a standard credit at session start and consumes it only when usable launch is established.

1. The standard monthly allocation is eight credits per learner, per app, per allocation month.
2. A bundle creates an independent eight-credit allocation for each included app assigned to the same learner.
3. Credits are not transferable, shareable, refundable as cash or usable for another learner/app.
4. Allocation month, weekly pacing and expiry use the learner's stored timezone. Version 1 defaults to Asia/Kolkata where no earlier valid learner timezone exists.
5. A full recurring allocation becomes effective at 00:00 on the first calendar day of the allocation month.
6. Each allocation expires at the end of the following calendar month in the same timezone.
7. Example: credits effective 1 August expire at the end of 30 September; credits effective 1 September expire at the end of 31 October.
8. Monthly allocations are materialized lazily when learner home, allowance read or session start first requires them.
9. Lazy creation preserves the original effective month and expiry; it does not use the row-creation timestamp as the grant date.
10. unique(learner_id, app_id, allocation_month) prevents duplicate monthly allocations.
11. Do not insert eight individual credit rows. Store one compact batch row with granted, reserved and consumed counts.
12. A recurring allocation is created only for a learner-app entitlement eligible for that allocation month. No inactive-month backfill is created.
13. Initial or partial-month subscription allocation is owned by the future billing/entitlement requirement and is not inferred by SC-002.
14. Existing unexpired credits continue ageing while entitlement is inactive, but no session may use them without an active entitlement.
15. Expired credits are never restored when entitlement resumes.
16. available_count = granted_count - reserved_count - consumed_count.
17. Reserved credits do not count as available.
18. Expiry is evaluated from server time and can be applied lazily; no midnight mass-update job is required.
19. Under the ordinary pacing rule, no more than two standard sessions may be funded for the learner/app in one server-derived calendar week.
20. The third-session catch-up rule is evaluated transactionally before reserving or consuming the third standard credit.
21. A third standard session is allowed only when all are true immediately before funding:
    a. exactly two standard sessions have already been funded in that learner/app/week;
    b. total available standard credits for the learner/app is greater than eight;
    c. at least one available standard-credit batch expires at the end of the current calendar month;
    d. the earliest-expiring available batch can fund the session;
    e. all ordinary account, entitlement, schedule, concurrency, deployment and authorization gates pass.
22. The catch-up rule is dynamic. Once available standard credits are eight or fewer, no further third standard session is allowed.
23. If no available credit expires in the current month, a balance above eight alone does not permit a third session.
24. No more than three standard sessions per learner/app/week may be funded.
25. A fourth standard session is always rejected.
26. Standard credit selection is automatic earliest-expiry-first; the learner does not choose a normal credit batch.
27. Technical replacement credits are separate. They are excluded from the standard available balance and standard weekly count.
28. Technical replacement credits retain the frozen LA-004 ability to bypass normal schedule and weekly pacing for the same learner/app.
29. Standard credit consumption and the learner-app weekly count occur atomically with the authoritative session-funding transaction.
30. Exact retries return the original funding result and never consume another credit or weekly count.
31. Concurrent starts lock the learner, weekly-usage row and relevant credit batches. At most one transaction consumes each unit.
32. A standard session stores the exact credit batch that funded it.
33. Resume never consumes another credit or increments weekly usage.
34. Finalization, interruption or technical-credit claim never restores the standard monthly credit.
35. A pre-usable-launch compensation rule may release a reserved standard credit only through the approved session-establishment contract; browser state cannot restore it.
36. Learner home displays total available standard credits, nearest expiry date, credits expiring this month, standard sessions used this week and whether a catch-up third session is currently eligible.
37. Learning apps do not receive the learner's full credit ledger; session funding is resolved before launch.
38. No direct learning-app database access or client-supplied balance/expiry/week values are accepted.
39. Allocation and expiry operations create only minimal audit/outbox data and no per-credit history.
40. Expired/exhausted old batch rows follow the approved commercial/usage retention policy and are not permanent learning analytics.
41. Session start increases reserved_count for the selected batch but does not increase consumed_count.
42. Weekly standard_sessions_funded increments only at SC-003 usable launch.
43. A five-minute reservation preserves the selected credit and proposed week/ordinal until activation or cancellation.
44. Reservation expiry/cancel decrements reserved_count; if the batch expired during the hold, the unit is expired rather than restored available.
45. A successful usable launch atomically decrements reserved_count, increments consumed_count and increments the reserved week usage.
46. Launch/exchange/browser initialization failures before usable launch consume no standard credit.

Authenticated Parent and Selected Learner Mode

As a parent, I want my account authority and each learner's learning authority to be clearly separated, so a learner can use only their selected profile after passkey unlock without accessing parent, billing or sibling information.

Babysteps shall use the authenticated parent session as the sole root end-user identity and shall enforce two mutually exclusive authorization modes within that session: parent-management mode and a passkey-unlocked learner mode bound to one selected learner and device. Every protected API shall derive the mode and exact learner/resource server-side and apply the AU-001 deny-by-default policy. Learner mode shall never grant or inherit parent, billing, learner-management, administrator or support authority.

1. Parent email/password authentication is the sole root end-user authentication in Version 1.
2. Parent-management mode exists after successful parent login unless an active learner_unlock_context places the browser/device in learner mode.
3. Learner mode is nested under the current parent session and cannot survive or exist without it.
4. Learner mode requires IA-004 passkey verification for the server-selected learner.
5. The authoritative learner-mode context is parent_session_id + device_session_id + learner_id + credential_id + expiry/version.
6. Client-selected mode, learner ID, parent ID, role, isParent, isLearner or permission fields have no authority.
7. Parent-management mode may access only the parent's own account, directly owned learners, purchased subscriptions, assigned entitlements, owned learner summaries and passkey management.
8. Parent-management mode may select an owned learner but cannot enter learner home/session start without that learner's passkey unlock.
9. Learner mode may access only the bound learner's safe learner home, app/credit/weekly availability, scheduled learning flow, safe progress summary, exact active/resumable session and eligible technical-issue confirmation.
10. Learner mode cannot access parent profile, contact details, security settings, account deletion, invoices, payments, subscription management, learner creation/correction, passkey management, another learner, administrator or support resources.
11. Learner mode cannot manually mutate progress, credit balances, entitlement, schedule or session funding.
12. Learning-app progress writes remain session-bound through LA-002/LA-003, not directly authorized by the browser learner mode.
13. A parent may view owned learner progress and commercial summaries in parent-management surfaces without entering learner mode.
14. Parent management never grants a learning session unless the selected learner has a valid learner unlock context and all domain gates pass.
15. Returning from learner mode to parent-management mode requires current parent-password reauthentication and revokes the learner context.
16. Selecting another learner revokes the current learner context and requires the new learner's passkey.
17. Parent logout, password/session revocation, suspension or soft deletion invalidates all nested learner contexts and session-start authority.
18. Passkey revocation invalidates active contexts created by that credential within five seconds.
19. A self-learner profile follows the same separation: parent mode manages; learner mode learns.
20. Matching parent and learner names, DOB or ownership never merges modes or privileges.
21. Parent list queries are scoped by owner_parent_id before count/pagination.
22. Learner-mode queries are scoped by bound learner_id before count/pagination.
23. Foreign parent/learner/resource IDs normally return non-enumerating RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.
24. Parent action on an owned resource may still be denied by domain rules such as entitlement, credit, schedule, deployment, account or concurrency.
25. Learner mode action on the bound learner may still be denied by the same domain rules.
26. Mutations authenticate, resolve canonical action/resource, preauthorize, lock authoritative state, reauthorize, validate business rules and commit atomically.
27. UI capability hints are advisory and never replace API authorization.
28. One parent session/device has only one active authorization mode and at most one learner context at a time.
29. Multiple devices under the same parent account maintain separate device-bound modes, but each still requires parent login and exact learner passkey.
30. Parent cannot use learner mode to avoid recent reauthentication for sensitive parent actions.
31. Learner mode cannot invoke internal app-service APIs or obtain platform/app service credentials.
32. Ordinary reads are not permanently audited; sensitive changes, mode transitions and denied cross-boundary attempts create minimal classified audit events.
33. Raw passkey responses, passwords, tokens, DOB, progress JSON, payment data and Runtime JSON are absent from authorization logs.
34. All actions use permanent canonical AU-001 action keys and typed context providers.
35. Unknown mode, missing context, stale context or authorization-provider failure denies by default.
