Babysteps Platform and Trusted Service Backends
Learning-App Backend and Automated Platform Service

As the Babysteps platform, I want every learning-app backend and automated workload to authenticate with its own short-lived, narrowly scoped machine identity so no app or job receives shared secrets or direct Supabase access.

Babysteps shall assign a distinct revocable machine principal to every learning-app backend and trusted automated workload in every environment. Machine principals authenticate using short-lived Ed25519-signed client assertions, receive only platform-assigned scopes and may call only documented Babysteps APIs. Private keys remain in the workload secret store; Babysteps stores public credentials only.

1. One service principal exists per workload and environment.
2. Learning apps, scheduled jobs, billing processors and deployment services never share a principal or credential.
3. Every learning-app principal is permanently bound to one canonical app_id and one environment.
4. Production, staging, preview and development identities are isolated.
5. Production private keys are never available to preview deployments, browsers, static JSON, curriculum assets or client bundles.
6. Use Ed25519/EdDSA asymmetric credentials in Version 1.
7. Babysteps stores only the public JWK, thumbprint, key ID, lifecycle status and safe metadata.
8. Babysteps never stores, returns or logs a machine private key.
9. Long-lived shared API keys, static bearer tokens, database passwords and Supabase service-role keys are prohibited for learning apps.
10. Every client assertion contains exact issuer/subject, audience, environment, issued/not-before/expiry times, random jti and principal version.
11. Learning-app assertions also contain canonical app_id, immutable deployment_id and contract version.
12. Client assertions expire within 60 seconds.
13. Assertion signature, algorithm, kid, issuer, subject, audience, environment, time window, jti, principal version, app and deployment are validated.
14. Accepted assertion jti hashes are retained only for assertion expiry plus a short replay window and then deleted.
15. Replayed assertions are rejected.
16. Successful authentication may issue a platform token lasting no more than five minutes.
17. LA-001/LA-002 remain authoritative for learning-app session grants and token renewal.
18. Generic non-session workload tokens are available only to approved internal service principals.
19. Scopes are assigned by Babysteps from an approved scope profile; the caller cannot add or expand scopes.
20. Learning-app scopes are limited to exact session-bound functions such as progress read/write, lesson completion, resume and completion.
21. Learning-app principals never receive parent, billing, subscription-management, admin, support, policy-management or direct database scopes.
22. A Magical Math principal cannot act as Chess Master, Speed Reader or any other app.
23. A principal cannot use another app's deployment, environment, session or grant.
24. Token audience is exact and one audience's token cannot call another service boundary.
25. Credential registration uses a short-lived proof-of-possession challenge.
26. The key pair is generated by the trusted workload/deployment process; only the public key is submitted.
27. Credential states are pending, active, retiring and revoked.
28. Pending credentials cannot authenticate.
29. Revoked credentials cannot be reactivated.
30. Zero-downtime rotation permits at most one active and one retiring credential for a principal.

32. Principal states are active, suspended and revoked.
33. Revoked principals cannot be reactivated and are retained while referenced.

Five-minute session reservation and usable-launch establishment
Babysteps Platform, Session Gateway and Learning-App SDK
Selected Learner, Session Gateway and Learning-App Backend
As a learner, I want my session credit to be consumed only after the learning app is actually ready, so a failed or abandoned launch does not waste a session while duplicate starts remain blocked.

Babysteps shall create a five-minute atomic session reservation before app launch. The reservation holds the exact learner lock, parent concurrency slot and selected standard or technical credit without increasing funded weekly usage. The session becomes active and permanently consumes the reserved credit only after the authenticated app launch succeeds and the browser runtime reports successful initialization through the app backend. If usable launch is not established within five minutes, the reservation is cancelled and all temporary holds are released.

1. POST session start creates status='starting' and funding_state='reserved'; it does not immediately create an active learning session.
2. Reservation lifetime is exactly five minutes from authoritative server reservation time.
3. reservation_expires_at = reserved_at + 300 seconds.
4. Start transaction revalidates exact learner mode, ownership, entitlement, schedule or technical credit, monthly availability, weekly pacing, learner lock, parent subscribed-learner concurrency ceiling, app and deployment.
5. Starting sessions count as the learner's single session and consume one parent concurrency slot while reserved.
6. A standard start reserves one unit from the earliest-expiring eligible monthly batch by increasing reserved_count only.
7. A technical-credit start changes the exact credit from available to reserved and binds it to the session.
8. Standard weekly funded usage is not increased during reservation.
9. The reserved week_key, timezone and proposed weekly ordinal are fixed at reservation time.
10. A credit valid when reserved remains eligible for usable launch until reservation_expires_at, even if its normal expiry occurs during the five-minute window.
11. Launch dispatch and app exchange must reference the exact starting session, selected app, deployment, device and reservation version.
12. Successful launch exchange alone does not consume the credit or start the 45-minute timer.
13. The learning-app browser must initialize the required IndexedDB runtime, claim one-tab ownership and establish its app-local session before usable launch confirmation.
14. The app backend confirms usable launch using LA-002 dual proof and the exact launch/runtime initialization context.
15. Usable-launch confirmation atomically changes starting→active and reserved→consumed.
16. The same transaction sets usable_launch_established_at and hard_expires_at = usable launch +3600 seconds.
17. The same transaction converts the standard batch reserved unit to consumed and increments the reserved week_key's funded count, or converts the bound technical credit reserved→consumed.
18. The 45 connected-minute browser timer begins only from usable_launch_established_at.
19. The signed SC-001 session envelope is issued only after usable launch succeeds.
20. Usable-launch confirmation is idempotent; identical retries return the original active session and envelope.
21. A conflicting usable-launch confirmation is rejected and cannot change app, learner, deployment, device, runtime version or funding.
22. A confirmation received after reservation expiry is rejected and triggers or observes cancellation.
23. Expired reservation cleanup atomically marks the session cancelled_before_launch, releases learner and parent concurrency locks, and releases the funding hold.
24. Releasing a standard reservation decrements reserved_count. If the batch has expired meanwhile, the unit becomes expired and is not restored as available.
25. Releasing a technical-credit reservation returns it to available only when it is still unexpired and otherwise marks it expired.
26. Reservation timeout never increments weekly funded usage.
27. Reservation timeout never creates progress, lesson completion, analytics session_started or technical-credit eligibility.
28. The learner may explicitly cancel a starting reservation before timeout; cancellation has the same release semantics.
29. Retrying session start with the same idempotency key returns the same reservation and never reserves a second credit.
30. After cancellation/expiry, the same old idempotency key returns the final cancelled result; a new start requires a new key.
31. A failed launch-dispatch, exchange, app authentication, browser initialization or usable-launch confirmation leaves the reservation intact only until its five-minute expiry.
32. Starting reservation cleanup is performed lazily during relevant reads/starts and by an indexed scheduled cleanup job; learner retry must not wait for the job.
33. Cleanup and usable-launch confirmation serialize so exactly one outcome wins.
34. No manual override, takeover or credit restoration occurs after usable launch.
35. Once active, SC-001/LA-003/LA-004 own runtime, progress and finalization; SC-003 no longer releases the consumed credit.
36. Parent logout, account inactivity, learner-context invalidation, entitlement revocation, app block or credential revocation before usable launch causes reservation cancellation unless an owning domain explicitly freezes a safer immediate denial outcome.
37. No browser-supplied time, credit batch, weekly ordinal, parent capacity or deployment is authoritative.
38. All state changes use server time, row locks, expected versions and exact idempotency.
39. Learning apps receive no direct credit ledger access.
40. No heartbeat is introduced.

Parent purchase, single-learner assignment and case-based administrator reassignment
Purchasing Parent and Authorized Billing Administrator

As a parent, I want to purchase an individual app or bundle for one selected learner, while preventing accidental self-service reassignment and allowing Babysteps administration to resolve legitimate assignment cases.

Babysteps shall create every subscription under one verified purchasing parent and bind it to exactly one owned learner selected before checkout confirmation. A parent cannot change the assigned learner through self-service after activation. Reassignment may occur only through a narrowly authorized administrator operation tied to an explicit case, with ownership, subscription, session, conflict and audit validation.

1. Every subscription has one immutable purchaser_parent_id.
2. Every subscription has exactly one assigned_learner_id while active or scheduled to activate.
3. The assigned learner must be directly owned by the purchasing parent at checkout.
4. The parent selects the learner before checkout and confirms learner name plus product before payment submission.
5. A product is either an individual-app product or a bundle product.
6. An individual-app product grants one app; a bundle grants its configured included apps to the same assigned learner.
7. One subscription never covers multiple learners.
8. A parent with multiple learners must purchase separate subscriptions for each learner requiring access.
9. The subscription assignment is not editable through parent self-service after activation.
10. Parent profile or learner selection state does not alter subscription assignment.
11. Learner rename or DOB correction does not change assignment because assignment uses immutable learner_id.
12. The purchaser parent may cancel the subscription under the later billing cancellation requirement, but cancellation does not reassign it.
13. The parent may submit or communicate a reassignment case to Babysteps administration.
14. BI-001 implements only a narrow subscription-reassignment case and action; it does not reactivate deferred AU-003 generic support administration.
15. Every reassignment requires a unique case_id, requesting parent, subscription, source learner, proposed target learner, reason and status.
16. The requesting parent must be the subscription purchaser and direct owner of both source and target learners.
17. The target learner must be active and belong to the same parent.
18. The subscription must be in an eligible current state and must not be permanently ended, refunded, charged back, disputed, suspended for fraud or owned by another parent.
19. The target learner must not already hold an overlapping active subscription that grants the same product/app access unless a later explicit consolidation rule exists.
20. Reassignment cannot occur while the source or target learner has a starting, active or resumable session in any affected app.
21. Reassignment never transfers learner identity, progress, lesson completions, mastery, achievements, historical usage or technical-session evidence.
22. Used, consumed or expired credits remain with the source learner and are never moved.
23. A reassignment requested after the subscription has produced usable learning access is scheduled for the next subscription period boundary by default.
24. Until the effective boundary, the source learner remains assigned and entitled.
25. At the effective boundary, the source learner's subscription-derived entitlements end and the target learner's entitlements begin atomically.
26. Initial target credit allocation and any partial-period exception are governed by the entitlement requirement; BI-001 does not duplicate or manually edit credit counters.
27. An administrator may correct the assignment immediately only when the subscription has not yet produced any usable learning session or consumed credit for the source learner.
28. Immediate correction before first use does not transfer progress because no learning use exists; downstream entitlements are rebuilt for the target through the entitlement service.
29. The administrator cannot directly edit purchaser_parent_id.
30. The administrator cannot assign the subscription to a learner owned by another parent.
31. The administrator cannot assign one subscription to multiple learners.
32. The administrator cannot bypass product, payment, entitlement, session or duplicate-access validation.
33. Reassignment requires exact billing administrator permission, recent reauthentication, case reason, expected subscription version and idempotency key.
34. The reassignment request and execution are audited with safe IDs and before/after learner IDs.
35. The parent cannot invoke the administrator reassignment endpoint.
36. A closed, rejected, expired or already executed case cannot authorize another reassignment.
37. Identical administrator retries return the original result; conflicting retries are rejected.
38. Subscription reassignment emits a versioned event for entitlement recalculation and session-access invalidation at the effective time.
39. Learning apps receive entitlements only through platform APIs and never read subscription records directly.
40. Subscription assignment is independent from the physical device used by the learner.
41. A bundle subscription counts as one subscription assigned to one learner but creates app entitlements according to its bundle contents.
42. Pricing, taxes, payment collection, refunds, cancellation timing and invoice generation are owned by later billing requirements.

values: Email/password only; Google plus email/password; passwordless magic link; phone OTP
Use email and password only for Version 1. Successful verified registration creates exactly one parent profile.
This minimizes implementation and support complexity, keeps one stable identity model across all apps and allows social providers to be added later without changing parent profile IDs.
Revisit when onboarding conversion data shows material authentication friction or when a platform requirement makes another provider necessary.
Parent profile fields and mobile verification
Optional or mandatory mobile; format validation only; SMS OTP verification; collect address/DOB; required or optional display name

Mobile number is mandatory and format-validated only with no SMS OTP. Display name is optional. Postal address and parent date of birth are not collected. Invoice delivery uses email and invoice label falls back to email when name is absent.
This supplies a parent contact number while minimizing cost, onboarding friction and personal-data collection. OTP can be introduced later only if a proven need emerges.
Revisit if phone ownership becomes necessary for security, communication delivery or fraud prevention.
Dynamic denominator; count only discovered requirements; establish a planning baseline
Track Version 1 progress against 76 planned requirements across 18 building blocks. Any count change must be explicitly recorded.
A stable denominator makes frozen, remaining and completion percentages meaningful while allowing controlled scope evolution.

Business requirements only; implementation notes in one column; dedicated exact build packet for every frozen requirement
Every frozen requirement must include an approved exact Codex build specification in 09_Codex_Build_Specs before it is marked Codex Ready.
Codex needs deterministic implementation contracts, technical boundaries, tests and exclusions to produce consistent code without inventing missing decisions.
Revisit only if the development agent accepts a superior structured contract format.
Email change and account deletion behavior
Hard delete; soft delete; old email active pending verification; immediate unverified swap; self/admin restoration

Use soft deletion only. Email verification expires in 24 hours; old email remains active until successful verification, then new email activates immediately and old email is archived. Restoration is administrator-controlled.
Retains operational, learning, billing and audit records while preventing access; verified email transition avoids losing account access.
Revisit only if legal retention/deletion obligations or product restoration policy change.
Windows-only PIN; separate Windows and Mac implementations; cross-platform WebAuthn; Must/Should/Nice classification
Create one cross-platform WebAuthn passkey requirement supporting Windows Hello and Apple/macOS passkeys. Classify it as Nice to Have.
WebAuthn provides one secure standard while keeping OS PIN/biometric data local. The feature is convenient but not required for launch.
Revisit when learner-device usage data justifies prioritizing passkey access.
Keep 76 requirements; add separate Windows and Mac requirements; add one cross-platform requirement
Increase the Version 1 planning baseline from 76 to 77 requirements and Identity from 3 to 4 planned requirements.

Separate household and membership tables; hidden auto-created household; direct parent ownership

Do not implement a household entity in Version 1. Retain household entity and membership scope as deferred future requirements. The stable parent profile UUID remains the ownership root for current learners and subscriptions.
This removes an invisible layer, duplicate authorization and onboarding complexity while preserving stable ownership independent of the mutable parent email.
Revisit if multiple adults must jointly own an inseparable family-wide entity or jointly owned subscription.
Household-owned subscription; learner-owned subscription; purchaser-parent-owned subscription

Every subscription belongs commercially to the parent who purchases it through purchaser_parent_id and is assigned to exactly one learner through assigned_learner_id. Learner entitlements are derived from that learner-specific subscription.

The paying parent is the commercial counterparty and invoice recipient, while the assigned learner is the sole beneficiary of that subscription. This keeps billing ownership and learner access explicit.
Revisit only if a separate institutional or jointly owned family subscription model is introduced.
Retain 77 planned requirements; replace household creation; remove requirement

Household-specific scope remains visible for future reconsideration without adding implementation work or distorting Version 1 completion.

Delete household scope entirely; keep it active; retain it as deferred future scope
Mark all household-specific requirements as Deferred. Exclude them from Version 1 planning, progress and Codex-ready counts.
The concept is not needed now, but retaining explicit deferred rows prevents accidental reintroduction and records what would require a future architecture decision.
Revisit only when a documented shared-family ownership or household-billing need is approved.
Subscription covers the parent account; subscription covers multiple learners; subscription covers exactly one assigned learner

Every subscription covers exactly one learner. The purchaser is the paying parent, recorded through purchaser_parent_id, and the covered learner is recorded through assigned_learner_id. An individual-app subscription grants that learner access to one app. A bundle subscription grants that same learner access to every app included in the bundle.

This supports independent app purchases and bundles while keeping access, pricing, renewals and usage unambiguous for each learner. A parent with multiple learners purchases or maintains separate learner-specific subscriptions.
Future Billing, Entitlement, Learner and Launcher requirements
Revisit only if Babysteps introduces family plans, transferable seats or institution-wide licensing.
Unlimited sessions; two sessions per learner across the platform; two sessions per learner per subscribed app

Each learner receives a maximum of two learning sessions per week for each app to which that learner has an active entitlement. The allowance is calculated independently for every learner-app pair. A bundle therefore provides two weekly sessions in each included app, not two sessions shared across the bundle.
The rule preserves the deliberate learning cadence while allowing a learner to study different subjects independently. It also avoids one app consuming another app's learning allowance.
Future Active Session Control, Entitlement, Engagement, Progress and Learning App contract requirements
Revisit only if learning-outcome evidence supports a different cadence or a product explicitly requires a different approved allowance.
Learner identity fields and name uniqueness
Display name only; legal name; duplicate names allowed; unique names per parent; age band; full date of birth

Require a familiar learner display name and date of birth. Display names are unique within the owning parent's active, paused and archived learner records after Unicode/case/whitespace normalization. Full legal name is not collected. There is no maximum learner age.
Unique names reduce wrong-learner selection and progress assignment. Date of birth gives developmental context while avoiding extra child identifiers.
Revisit naming or DOB collection only if usability, privacy or supported-market requirements change. Adult learner eligibility is permanent unless explicitly superseded.
Age determines curriculum; mastery only; age adjusts presentation while mastery determines progression; retained learners remain accessible after owner deletion

Use derived age to tailor presentation, scaffolding and delivery speed, while mastery remains authoritative for readiness and progression. When the owning parent is soft deleted, all learner-profile, app-launch, passkey and progress access is denied although records remain retained.
This supports age-appropriate delivery without holding back advanced younger learners or advancing unready older learners, and preserves the account soft-delete security boundary.
Revisit only through an approved pedagogy or account-continuity change.
Child-only learner profiles; capped learner age; adults allowed; parent allowed as learner

Any person with a valid non-future date of birth may have a learner profile. There is no maximum learner age. The paying parent may create a learner profile for themselves using the same direct-ownership model.

Babysteps learning products can serve children and adults. A separate self-learner identity or ownership model is unnecessary because the learner UUID already separates learning progress from the parent login identity.
LP-001 and all app adaptation contracts
Revisit only if a particular product has a separately approved minimum-age safety restriction; such a restriction must apply at app entitlement/launch rather than platform learner creation.
Permanent learner identity and lifecycle scope
Pause/archive/delete lifecycle; archive only; permanent learner record with correction only
Learner profiles are permanent Version 1 identities. Do not implement pause, archive, restore, hide or delete. Subscriptions and entitlements alone determine app access.
Lifecycle states would duplicate commercial access controls and create unnecessary status, revocation and restoration complexity.
LP-001, LP-002 and all learner-access requirements
Revisit only if a documented operational need cannot be solved through profile correction, subscription validity or support tooling.
Delete mistaken learner; archive; admin correction; owner correction of profile fields

Profile correction handles entry mistakes with the smallest safe surface while preserving a stable cross-app identity.
Revisit only if evidence shows a required correction cannot be represented by the three editable fields.
Implement at launch; implement simple shared access; defer outside Version 1
Defer LP-003 additional guardian access outside the Version 1 baseline. Version 1 keeps exactly one owning parent per learner and uses direct owner_parent_id authorization only.

Secure multi-adult access requires invitation security, child-data consent, permission boundaries, immediate revocation, session invalidation and family-dispute support. This complexity is not necessary for the initial product.
Revisit only when validated demand for multiple-adult learner management justifies a complete requirement and Codex packet.
Learner selection and scheduled app entry
Parent-wide app list; automatic last learner; explicit learner first

A multi-learner parent must explicitly select a learner before learner home. A single learner may auto-select. Learner home shows only that learner's entitled apps and enables only the centrally scheduled app.
Explicit selection and server-bound learner UUID prevent cross-learner progress and subscription mistakes while preserving a simple learner journey.
Revisit only if a future learner-direct login safely establishes the same learner context.
Concurrent learner sessions and override policy
Parent count only; replace old session; user takeover; strict one session with no override

Each learner may have at most one starting, active or resumable learning session across all apps/devices. A parent with N learners can therefore have at most N concurrent reserved sessions. Another device is blocked and no user override or takeover is permitted.
A late takeover could discard nearly completed learning and unfairly consume another weekly session. Strict learner locking protects progress and cadence.
Only an authorized administrator may revoke a session for support/security; this does not create automatic replacement eligibility.
Immediate loss; fresh session; unlimited reconnect; 15-minute same-session resume plus admin review

An accidentally disconnected session may resume on the original device/browser within a cumulative 15-minute recovery allowance without consuming another slot. At 50% or more verified active time it is conclusively used. Below 50% remains consumed unless an administrator grants one audited replacement credit after evidence review.
This protects genuine browser/network interruptions without enabling device switching, repeated extension or automatic extra sessions.
Revisit heartbeat/activity calculation only from operational evidence; the no-override and 50% policy remain explicit decisions.
Migration only; developer self-registration; Version 1 admin page
Provide /admin/apps from Version 1. Authorized administrators create draft apps, edit metadata, activate and restore them. App UUID and app_key are permanent.
A controlled admin workflow supports adding apps without deployments while keeping the platform as the trust authority.
Developer self-service remains excluded until a future reviewed requirement.
Hard and soft delete; hard delete unused apps; soft delete only
Soft deletion is the only app removal mechanism. No hard-delete API, UI, SQL routine or cascade exists. Minimal permanent app identity remains to preserve references.
An app row is negligible compared with operational data; physical deletion risks corrupting progress, billing and analytics interpretation.
Do not revisit physical deletion unless the entire referential and legal model changes.
Permanent events; compact summaries; current state plus completions

Named learner storage is limited to current app progress, lessons completed and data temporarily required for an active/resumable session or explicit support case. Repeated progress snapshots and permanent raw session/event histories are prohibited.
This preserves learning continuity while preventing database growth and unnecessary learner surveillance.
AN-001, progress, sessions, privacy and support
Any new retained field must state its operational purpose and deletion trigger.
Real-time event warehouse; no analytics; daily temporary buffer and aggregate

Maintain one temporary daily pseudonymous buffer and run one aggregation at 00:15 Asia/Kolkata for the previous date. Write anonymous app/level/age-band aggregates, verify totals and delete all daily source pseudonyms.
The design answers product questions about time, levels and age groups without permanent identifiable histories.
Broader distributions or real-time analytics require a separate approved privacy/data-minimization decision.
Manual environment URLs; admin-edited production origin; automated provider deployment
Deployment origins and launch configuration are generated from a provider-verified deployment and versioned app manifest. Administrators cannot enter or edit the live production URL.
Removing free-text production configuration prevents typos, malicious redirects and environment drift.
AR-002, BB-04 and all app launches
A new provider must implement the same verification adapter contract.
Rebuild per environment; automatic merge-to-production; build once plus explicit approval
Build one immutable artifact, validate it in staging and promote the same digest to production after explicit authorized approval. Do not expose every successful merge automatically.
The same artifact prevents environment drift, while approval catches technically valid but pedagogically or operationally unsuitable releases.
Approval automation may be reconsidered only after strong production evidence and an explicit risk decision.
Provider deployment immediately live; redirect all sessions; atomic pointer and previous-release rollback

The platform atomically publishes a verified deployment for new launches, keeps active sessions on their original deployment and retains the previous healthy release for automated or authorized rollback.
Separating provider deployment from learner publication prevents partial exposure and protects work already in progress.
Version 1 stops at the ten-minute AR-002 release-safety window. Continuous monitoring, maintenance and retirement controls are deferred.
Implement in Version 1; implement only health polling; defer full availability/maintenance/retirement controls

Defer AR-003 outside the Version 1 baseline. Version 1 retains deployment-time validation, the ten-minute post-publication safety window and automated/manual rollback from AR-002, but excludes continuous monitoring, maintenance scheduling, emergency availability state and planned retirement orchestration.
These controls are operationally valuable but do not block initial learner journeys. Deferral avoids a premature state machine, monitoring service and billing/communication coordination surface.
Revisit after Version 1 usage or when scheduled maintenance, recurring outages or planned app retirement becomes an evidenced operational need.
Permit breaking releases; support only N-1; require compatibility with represented retained data

Every release must preserve current platform contracts and provide tested read/migration compatibility for every progress schema version present in retained learner progress. Use expand/migrate/contract and block destructive same-step changes.
Inactive learners may return with older current progress. A release that only supports the previous code version can still strand real learner data.
Contract removal is allowed only after data is migrated, no retained row requires it and rollback safety is explicitly verified.
Deploy while learners study; platform-wide outage; app-specific 60-minute drain and slot

Every production deployment uses an app-specific scheduled slot. New sessions for that app are blocked from 60 minutes before the slot until safe publication or rollback, and deployment begins only when zero reserved sessions remain. Other apps continue normally.
A 45-minute session plus 15-minute same-device recovery requires a 60-minute drain to guarantee no learning session overlaps deployment.
This narrow deployment control does not activate deferred AR-003 maintenance and continuous availability functionality.
URL JWT; shared cookie; reusable platform token; one-time POST code and backend exchange

Use a 60-second opaque single-use code sent by exact cross-origin POST and exchanged by an app/deployment-bound confidential backend for a 120-second minimal bootstrap assertion. The app creates its own learner-only local session.
This prevents browser token leakage, app impersonation, parent credential sharing and cross-app session confusion.
Longer-lived app-to-platform API authorization, progress/completion and logout are separate BB-04 requirements.
Bearer token only; app credential only; dual session token and app assertion
Every protected app-to-platform request requires a short session-bound access token and a fresh app/environment/deployment-bound service assertion. Neither credential is sufficient alone.
Dual proof limits both stolen-token use and misuse by a compromised app backend against another learner session.
LA-002 and all protected app APIs
Do not weaken to browser tokens or shared app secrets.
Long-lived refresh token; bootstrap assertion reuse; <=5m token with no refresh and immediate grant checks

Use backend-only access tokens lasting at most five minutes, renewed against the active grant and central session with no refresh token. Check grant version/status on every call and purge grant/renewal state after purpose.
Short credentials plus immediate grant checks support lifecycle revocation while meeting the minimum-data rule.
Longer-lived offline app access is outside Version 1.

BOUNDARIES
Babysteps owns learner selection, launch authorization, session concurrency/timing, weekly usage, resume and replacement-credit consumption. Apps own pedagogy/content and provide a signed schedule authorization through the approved scheduler contract. Do not calculate curriculum order here.

DATABASE

- normal_sessions_started between 0 and 2.
- Unique normal weekly_slot_number 1 or 2 per learner/app/week.
- Unique replacement_credit_id consumption.

WEEK
Calculate ISO week server-side in learner stored timezone, Monday 00:00. Persist week_key/week_timezone at start. Do not accept client week. Timezone changes take effect only next week boundary.

SELECTION
GET /v1/learner-selection and PUT /v1/learner-selection.
Zero learners -> creation. One -> auto-select. More than one -> explicit card selection after each new parent login. Store against current parent auth session only and clear with it.

START
POST /v1/learner-sessions/start strict payload learnerId, appId, scheduleAuthorization, idempotencyKey. Device ID comes from secure random cookie.
In one serializable transaction:
1 active account and exact owner/bound learner.
2 selected learner context.
3 valid entitlement.
4 verify signed current schedule authorization for same learner/app.
5 lock/finalize stale learner session state.
6 reject if any starting/active/disconnected session remains.
7 lock learner-app-week usage.
8 allocate normal slot 1/2, else select a matching valid replacement credit; otherwise reject.
9 create starting then active learner session and exact-once result.
10 write audit/outbox.
Never override, terminate or supersede an ongoing session.

SESSION CLOCK
Maximum connected_elapsed_seconds 2700. Client heartbeat every 30 seconds. Server calculates increments from server timestamps and monotonic sequence; client totals are advisory/ignored. Track verified_active_seconds separately for support threshold. Complete at 2700 seconds or valid app completion.

DISCONNECT/RESUME
Best-effort authenticated disconnect beacon plus heartbeat timeout fallback.
Disconnected session remains the unique learner lock.
First/repeated resume requires original device ID and hashed resume credential.
Cumulative disconnected time max 900 seconds. Effective resume deadline is disconnected_at plus remaining allowance, never more than 15 minutes.
Resume reuses same session, week, app and weekly slot; no new row or usage.
Different device cannot resume and cannot override.
Sweeper finalizes expired disconnected sessions as interrupted; start/resume paths also lazily finalize.

WEEKLY USE AND SUPPORT
Normal slot is consumed at start exactly once.
verified_active_seconds >= 1350 is conclusively used and replacement-ineligible.
Below 1350 remains consumed and is not automatically restored. UI offers Contact support.
Administration may create one audited replacement credit per original session after evidence review. LP-004 only consumes available unexpired matching credit. Replacement start still requires entitlement, schedule and no concurrent learner session.

TOKENS/PROGRESS
Learning tokens are signed, short-lived and scoped to session, learner, app and device. Progress write requires active exact-bound session. Ended/foreign tokens denied. Parent soft deletion immediately blocks selection/home/start/resume/heartbeat/progress.

values: These approved decisions must be incorporated verbatim into the later Codex-ready Billing, Entitlement, Session and Learning App contract requirements.

A subscription has exactly one purchaser parent and exactly one assigned learner. An individual-app product grants only its app. A bundle product grants every included app to the same assigned learner. The same subscription never covers a second learner.

subscriptions.purchaser_parent_id NOT NULL; subscriptions.assigned_learner_id NOT NULL; subscriptions.product_id NOT NULL. products.product_type in individual_app|bundle. Product-to-app mapping defines granted apps.
Billing owns subscription lifecycle. Entitlements expand the product into learner-app access rows. Learning apps consume entitlements and never infer subscription coverage.

Parent owns multiple learners; parent buys multiple subscriptions; individual app overlaps bundle; cancellation/expiry; product app removed; duplicate entitlement sources; permanent learner with no current entitlement; payment failure.
No parent-wide or family-wide coverage. No shared learner seats. No household billing. No automatic reassignment between learners. Reassignment policy remains a separate future decision.
Two weekly sessions per learner per app

For every active learner-app entitlement, the learner has two normal learning-session starts in each server-defined week. Counters are independent by learner_id and app_id. A normal slot is consumed atomically at start. A bundle gives two normal sessions in each included app. Only an available audited administrator replacement credit may authorize an additional same-learner/app session.

Weekly usage key includes learner_id, app_id, week_key and week_timezone. learner_app_week_usage.normal_sessions_started is constrained to 0–2. Normal learner_sessions carry weekly_slot_number 1 or 2. Replacement sessions carry one unique replacement_credit_id instead of a normal slot.

Central platform authorizes session start and returns remaining weekly allowance. Each learning app must request authorization before starting a qualifying learning session and must report start/end state.

Third normal attempt; learner has multiple apps; bundle; overlapping subscription sources; week boundary; duplicate start; active/disconnected learner lock; browser interruption/resume; replacement credit validity; entitlement or schedule loss.
No shared platform-wide pool. No transfer/carry-forward. No reset from device change/reinstall. No app-local source of truth. No automatic restoration. No product or user override.
Explicit learner selection and scheduled launch

More than one learner requires explicit selection for each new parent login; one learner may auto-select. Learner home is scoped to selected learner and only the current signed scheduled app can start.

learner_selection_contexts is keyed by parent_session_id and selected_learner_id. Every launch/session/progress contract contains immutable learner_id and app_id. Schedule authorization is server signed and short-lived.
Unified launcher owns selection/home. Scheduler owns which app is due. Session gateway revalidates ownership, entitlement and schedule before start.
Zero/one/multiple learners; session expiry; parent switches learner; similar names; stale schedule; no entitlement; other learner sessions running.
No parent-wide combined app launcher. No name-based progress ownership. No launcher-computed pedagogy schedule. No cross-learner data response.
One learner session, no override, safe resume

Each learner has at most one starting, active or disconnected learning session across all apps/devices. Another device cannot override it. The original device/browser may resume the same session within a cumulative 900-second disconnection allowance; no new slot is consumed.

learner_sessions partial unique learner_id for reserved statuses; random device_session_id; hashed resume credential; 30-second heartbeat; connected time cap 2700; cumulative disconnected cap 900; verified-active threshold 1350. Finalized session detail is purged after compact progress/completion/analytics propagation and any explicit support-case retention.
Central session gateway owns start, heartbeat, disconnect, resume and completion. Apps never create/replace sessions locally. Administration alone grants replacement credits after logs review.
Browser close; crash; network loss; missed heartbeat; repeated interruptions; second device; different app; second weekly session active; recovery crosses week boundary; stale sweeper.
No user takeover, supersede or end-other-session. No cross-device resume. No disconnected time counted as learning. No automatic credit below 50%. No credit at or above 50%.
Every app is created through the Version 1 admin registry with immutable UUID/app_key. Soft deletion is the only removal action; it blocks new operation but preserves minimal identity and references.
app_registry with draft|active|soft_deleted, version and RESTRICT foreign keys. No hard-delete route/function/cascade. All relationships use app_id.
App Registry owns identity/state. Downstream services reject non-active apps and consume invalidation events.
Duplicate key; stale admin edit; missing activation configuration; active subscriptions; soft delete/restore; unknown app; downstream invalidation failure.
No physical delete, key reuse, browser/developer self-registration or display-name/URL identity.

Retain named data only for current learner-app progress, unique lessons completed, active/resumable session operation and explicit temporary support needs. Do not keep repeated progress snapshots or permanent raw interaction/session histories.
One learner_app_progress row per learner/app; one lesson_completions row per learner/app/lesson; current session updated in place; every temporary table has deletion trigger.
Progress owns continuation/completion. Session owns current operation. Analytics owns only temporary daily source and anonymous aggregates.
Interrupted support review; retries; crash recovery; cross-midnight session; deleted app; learner/parent account state.
No clickstream, heartbeat rows, session replay, answer-by-answer history by default, permanent daily pseudonyms or indefinite operational logs.
At 00:15 Asia/Kolkata process the explicit previous date, exact-replace app/level/age-band aggregates, verify control totals and delete all temporary learner daily keys/source rows.
Temporary HMAC daily buffer; anonymous analytics_daily_level/app; compact run row. No learner/parent IDs, names, DOB or exact age in permanent analytics.
Trusted contribution service and scheduler own writes/runs. Admin reads completed cohorts only. Analytics never controls learner state.
Concurrent/missed/failed run; midnight split; replay; deletion failure; soft-deleted app; missing secret; active learner across levels.
No raw event warehouse, browser ingestion, named admin drilldown, client-owned time or permanent source pseudonyms.

Apps are built once into immutable releases, automatically deployed and validated, explicitly approved for production, atomically published for new sessions and automatically rollback-capable. No administrator or browser may enter a live production URL.

Verified provider binding; validated app manifest; immutable commit/lock/build hashes and artifact digest; current/previous deployment publication pointer; active session records deployment ID temporarily. Production deployment additionally requires a passed compatibility report and app-specific deployment window.

Deployment pipeline owns build, compatibility, scheduled drain/window, staging and provider work. App Registry owns identity. Launch/session services consume only published deployment and deployment-start block.
Wrong project/repository/domain; manifest mismatch; failed gates; concurrent promotions; production smoke failure; active session during publish; webhook replay; soft-deleted app; rollback failure.
No manual production URL, environment rebuild, merge-direct-to-learners, direct repository pointer mutation, session redirection or permanent preview/build-log archive.

Every production release supports current platform contracts and all progress schema versions represented in retained data. Deployment is app-specific and scheduled >=60 minutes ahead; starts are blocked from the 60-minute drain through safe publication/rollback; deployment begins only at zero reserved sessions.
app_release_compatibility_reports; app_deployment_windows; session-start checks app/time/status; no usage mutation on block; expand/migrate/contract migrations.
Deployment pipeline owns compatibility and window. LP-004 start transaction and LA-001 dispatch consume the block. Other apps are unaffected.
Old progress schema; destructive migration; active/disconnected session at slot; overlapping window; overrun; rollback; concurrent start at drain boundary.
No breaking release, deployment during learner session, platform-wide blackout, user override, automatic slot consumption or full AR-003 maintenance state.

An authorized learner session launches through a 60-second opaque single-use POST code exchanged only by the exact app/environment/deployment backend for a 120-second minimal bootstrap assertion and app-local learner session.
One mutable learner_session_launch_state; scoped app_service_principals; short exchange receipts; session app/deployment/release/device binding; hash-only code.
Platform dispatch/exchange own trust. App backend verifies assertion and owns local cookie. LP-004 owns session/allowance. AR-002 owns deployment/compatibility/window.
Expired/replayed/revoked code; lost response; wrong app/env/deployment/device; deployment drain; compatibility failure; new release publication; account/app deletion.
No URL token, shared cookie/secret, parent token, browser exchange, cross-app launch, parent privilege, direct platform DB access or permanent attempt history.

Every protected app-to-platform call uses a backend-only access token lasting <=5 minutes plus a fresh replay-protected app assertion. The grant is exact learner/session/app/deployment bound, fixed-scope, immediately revocable and has no refresh token.
Unique app_session_grants; short renewal receipts; token grant/version/session/principal/scopes/contract claims; raw token absent; temporary rows purge.
LA-001 creates initial grant. App backend owns token cache. Platform middleware validates both proofs. LP-004/account/app lifecycle revokes. AR-002 requires zero grants for deployment.
Expired token with valid grant; original-device resume; wrong principal/binding; scope failure; account/app deletion; key rotation; deployment drain; transaction failure.
No browser token, refresh token, broad scope, parent/admin access, direct DB, permanent token history or token-carried personal/progress data.
